allowed_dependency_manifest.content: Let n, k, l ∈ Z with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n. Define R(q) = [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q in the natural rational-function setting for Gaussian q-binomial coefficients. If R(q) lies in a polynomial ring in q (i.e., R(q) has only finitely many nonnegative powers of q with coefficients in the relevant coefficient ring), then when written as R(q) = Σ_i c_i q^i, every coefficient c_i satisfies c_i ≥ 0.

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260324204708_474b5c77
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For integers A, B, d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define Q_{A,B,d}(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when d = 0. Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) belongs to Q[q]. Let S be the weighted polynomial ring Q[x_1, ..., x_d] graded by deg(x_i) = B+i; when d = 0 interpret S as Q. Then there exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that deg(f_i) = A+i for every i, and for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1, ..., f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, Q_{A,B,d}(q) is realized by a homogeneous regular sequence in a weighted polynomial ring with variable weights B+1, ..., B+d and relation degrees A+1, ..., A+d.

payload.statement_nl: Let A,B be integers with A >= B >= 0. For d=0 one has Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1, the weighted polynomial ring is S=Q, and the empty sequence of elements of S is a homogeneous regular sequence. Its quotient is S itself, whose Hilbert series is 1.

notes: No ancestor lemma or root theorem claim was cited.
The proof uses only the empty-product convention, zero-variable polynomial ring convention, standard regular-sequence vacuity, and the standard definition of Hilbert series.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix integers A,B with A >= B >= 0, and set d=0.

By the meaning of Q_{A,B,d}(q), the case d=0 is a product over an empty index set. By the standard convention for empty products, this gives Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1.

For d=0 the weighted polynomial ring has no variables. A polynomial ring over Q in zero variables is just Q itself, so S=Q. In this zero-variable case the grading is trivial: S_0=Q and S_m=0 for every m>0.

Now consider the empty sequence in S. There are no terms at all, so the homogeneity conditions and the non-zero-divisor conditions in the definition of a homogeneous regular sequence are vacuous. Moreover, if one includes the usual nontriviality requirement for a regular sequence, it is satisfied because the quotient by the ideal generated by the empty sequence is S/(0)=S=Q, which is nonzero. Hence the empty sequence is a homogeneous regular sequence.

Since the ideal generated by the empty sequence is the zero ideal, its quotient is S itself.

Finally, the Hilbert series of S is
H_S(q)=sum_{m>=0} (dim_Q S_m) q^m.
Because S_0=Q has dimension 1 over Q and S_m=0 for all m>0, we get
H_S(q)=1.

Therefore, for d=0, we have Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1, the weighted polynomial ring is S=Q, the empty sequence of elements of S is a homogeneous regular sequence, its quotient is S itself, and that quotient has Hilbert series 1. This is exactly the statement.
result_payload.proof_summary: In the case d=0, Q_{A,B,0}(q) is an empty product, hence 1. The weighted polynomial ring has no variables, so it is Q. The empty sequence is vacuously homogeneous and regular, it generates the zero ideal, so its quotient is S itself, and since S=Q is concentrated in degree 0, its Hilbert series is 1.

used_external_facts: Standard convention that an empty product equals 1
A polynomial ring over Q with zero variables is Q
The empty sequence is vacuously a homogeneous regular sequence (and its quotient is nonzero here)
The Hilbert series of Q concentrated in degree 0 is 1
